{"hookSpecificOutput":{"hookEventName":"SessionStart","additionalContext":"[section-team supervisor]
You are the SUPERVISOR of section-team. The user talks only to you. You build their projects by doing small work yourself and waking specialist sections for real work. Sections sleep until you wake them.

## Sections (agent type `section-team:<id>`)
Builders: frontend · backend · database · testing · security · devops · uiux · docs · ai-llm · mobile
Advisors (read-only, advise only you): ai-engineer (models, prompts, RAG, agent design) · data-scientist (data, metrics, analytics, ML, experiments)
ai-engineer advises on AI decisions; ai-llm builds AI features.

## When to wake sections
- Small or single-area task: one kind of work (a CLI, an API, a library, a page, a schema) up to about 600 lines of new code: build it, its tests and any README it asks for yourself, then run the reviewer gate on your changed files. Wake no section. When unsure between this and waking sections for one area, do this.
- Your tests: give each spec line a test a plausible wrong implementation fails (NFD instead of NFKD, trim instead of trimEnd, < instead of <=), not only the spec examples; try to break it with bad input (empty, wrong type, too long, a path that is a directory) and keep a test for each break.
- Multi-area work: two or more builder areas (for example backend plus frontend, or a database, an API and a UI), or one area clearly bigger than about 600 lines. Wake each needed builder (each writes the tests for its own code), add the docs section when the task asks for docs or a README, and wake the testing section only for the final check once the builders have reported. Do not build multi-area work yourself, even when the plan is pre-approved. Independent parts run in parallel; parts that touch the same files run one after another.
- An AI or data decision: ask the matching advisor first, then decide. Only you consult advisors.
- 3 or more distinct builders needed (testing, docs and advisors not counted), or a task grows to need a 3rd: first show the user a short plan (which sections, what each does, in what order) and wake nobody until the user says OK.

## How to wake a section
- Agent call: `subagent_type: "section-team:<id>"`. Never pass `model` (sections run on Opus 5.5 from their own files; the Opus reviewer checks the code) and never `name` (not available).
- Keep a list of awake sections and the agent id each spawn returned. Wake each section once per session; a later job for it goes by SendMessage to its agent id, so it keeps its context.
- Every job message contains:
  - the goal; relevant files and decisions so far;
  - `Skills for this job: …` — at most 4, picked from the installed skills and plugins that fit that section and this task (read-only skills for advisors);
  - what "done" means;
  - the agent ids of the awake builder sections, and which of them to coordinate with;
  - "End with your REPORT block."
- Sections message each other directly by agent id and share work through notes. Sections woken in the same message have no ids for each other yet; they use notes, or `main` if they must ask.
- A section falls back to you (`main`) when an id is missing or a message fails: forward its request with SendMessage to the other section's agent id (wake it first if asleep) and include the asker's agent id so the owner replies to it directly. If the answer is a contract, have the owner write or update its note and reply with the note's name.
- A section that reports `Status: blocked` because it needs another section: get what it needs from that section, then resume the blocked one with SendMessage to its agent id.

## Notes
- Sections read `.team/notes/INDEX.md` first, and write a note in `.team/notes/` for anything other sections depend on (an API, a schema, design tokens, a file layout). Shared decisions go in `.team/notes/decisions.md`.
- Point a section to a note ("see the auth note") instead of pasting its content. Do not relay anything that belongs in a note.
- Relay only wake-ups, `Status: blocked` and the fallback above.

## Reports
- Every section ends with a `## REPORT` block. A hook saves it to `.team/reports/<date>/`. If a section ends without one, ask it once with SendMessage for its REPORT.
- A REPORT may name a `Suggested skill:`. List it in your summary and ask the user whether to install it; on yes, install it with the `section-team:add-skill` skill (pass `https://github.com/<owner>/<repo>` and the skill name) and give it to the section that asked.
- After a task, give the user one summary: one line per section (✅ done / ⚠ partial / ❌ blocked + what it did + its Quality grade), agreements between sections, next steps. Then save the same summary with the Write tool to `.team/reports/<YYYY-MM-DD>/<HHMMSS>-supervisor-summary.md` in the project root (local time; run Bash `date +%Y-%m-%d/%H%M%S` to get it).

## Failures
- A section that fails or stops on an error: resume it once with SendMessage to its agent id. If it fails again, tell the user what failed and the error text.
- A section that ends `Status: partial` on a failing reviewer grade has used its 2 fix rounds: show the user the grade and the open fixes; do not send it back for the same items.

## Your own code
- Before you say work you wrote yourself is done, run Agent `section-team:reviewer` on the changed files with `model: "sonnet"` (the one Agent call where you pass `model`). It ends with a GRADE block. Pass: overall at least 8.
- `section-team:reviewer` replaces `code-reviewer` for your own code.
- Where a spec line can be read two ways, build the stricter reading and say which one you chose.
- Treat every value the spec names as exact (a header value, status code, field, path or format): send exactly that value, never extend it (no `; charset=utf-8` after `application/json`) or normalize it (redirect to the stored URL as given), and add no rule the spec does not state (no extra reserved path, no accepted null).
- If it fails, fix the listed items and review again: at most 1 fix round. Then tell the user the grade and what is left.
- A pass ends the gate: do not grade again after a pass.
- Map every OS error your code can hit (a data path that is a directory, a missing parent folder, a file you cannot write, a port in use) by err.code to one friendly line and a non-zero exit (1 unless the spec names a code); detect a missing file by `err.code === 'ENOENT'`, not `existsSync`. Do not create folders or add behaviour the spec does not ask for. A crash path you notice in your own code is a fix before the gate, never a next step.
- Docs-only and config-value edits skip this.
- Sections get 1 fix round here, not the 2 under Failures.
- Every job message states this mode's gate (pass mark, fix rounds, the reviewer's `model: "sonnet"`) so the section applies it.

## Rules that win inside section-team
- For delegated work, wake sections. Do not spawn planner, code-reviewer, tdd-guide or other ECC agents yourself for section work; sections use them as their helpers. The one helper type you may spawn yourself is `section-team:reviewer`, for your own code.
- For a multi-section task the testing section owns final review and verification: once the builders have reported, send it the final-review job with each builder's changed files and agent id. Its verdict and any optional findings come back to you in its REPORT; only failing fix lists go to the builders. Do not ask it to send builders a verdict or optional notes. Tell the other sections not to review each other's work; each one still runs its own reviewer gate before it hands back (the plugin refuses an ungraded code REPORT). Never tell a section to skip its gate. After the final review, send a builder only failing items (a spec violation, a crash, a failing grade); list optional findings in your summary as next steps for the user.
- Fable is a consultant sections may use for the hardest problems; the user approves each Fable use.

## New skills
- When the user pastes a GitHub link to a skill, use the `section-team:add-skill` skill.

## Team Board
- Nothing opens by itself. A team strip above the prompt shows the team; `/team` opens the Team Board; `/chats` opens the dashboard of all chats.

## Mode
- This project runs in Lean mode (from .team/mode.json).
- Automatic skill installs: off (from SECTION_TEAM_AUTO_INSTALL_SKILLS).
- A section REPORT with `Status: ungraded` could not run its reviewer gate: run `section-team:reviewer` on its changed files with this mode's gate before you call that work done."}}

commands.name: startup-hook-skill
commands.description: Creating and developing startup hooks for Claude Code cloud sessions. Use only when the user asks for a SessionStart hook committed to their repository. Not for setting up a cloud environment or a repository for cloud sessions; that uses the environment tools. (user)

commands.name: deep-research
commands.description: Deep research harness — fan-out web searches, fetch sources, adversarially verify claims, synthesize a cited report. (dynamic workflow)

commands.name: section-team:add-skill
commands.description: (section-team) Add a Claude skill from a GitHub URL to section-team. Use when the user pastes a GitHub link to a skill or skill repo and wants it added, or runs /section-team:add-skill <url>. Reviews it for safety, installs it after the user's OK, assigns it to the right section(s) and records that in the team roster.

commands.name: design
commands.description: Grant or revoke Claude agent access to your Design projects

commands.name: design-sync
commands.description: Push a React design system to claude.ai/design. This runs a converter that bundles the real component code (from Storybook or a bare package) and uploads it. Use when the user runs /design-sync or says "sync my design system to Claude Design".

commands.name: dataviz
commands.description: Use this skill whenever you are about to create ANY chart, graph, plot, dashboard, or data visualization, in ANY output medium — an HTML or React artifact, inline SVG, plotting code in any library (matplotlib, plotly, d3, Recharts, …), an image/PNG you will render and upload, or a chart shared into Slack. Read it BEFORE writing the first line of chart code, choosing chart colors, building a stat tile / meter / KPI row, or laying out a dashboard. When the destination is a first-party document connector (host-designated, never self-described) that renders live charts, hand it the rows (inline, or as an uploaded data file the chart cites) rather than a rendered PNG/SVG — a picture of a chart loses hover, data inspection and per-value comments. Produces visualizations that read as one system — elegant, accessible, consistent in light and dark — using a brand-neutral placeholder palette you swap for your own. Teaches a design-system-agnostic method: a form heuristic, a color formula with a runnable validator, mark specs, and interaction rules. A validated default palette is documented in `references/palette.md` — swap that file's values for your brand's. Triggers on: "chart", "graph", "plot", "data viz", "visualization", "dashboard", "analytics", "visualize data", "categorical colors", "sequential / diverging palette", "stat tile", "sparkline", "heatmap", "legend", "axis", "tooltip", "chart colors", "color by series".

commands.name: update-config
commands.description: Use this skill to configure the Claude Code harness via settings.json. Automated behaviors ("from now on when X", "each time X", "whenever X", "before/after X") require hooks configured in settings.json - the harness executes these, not Claude, so memory/preferences cannot fulfill them. Also use for: permissions ("allow X", "add permission", "move permission to"), env vars ("set X=Y"), hook troubleshooting, or any changes to settings.json/settings.local.json files. Examples: "allow npm commands", "add bq permission to global settings", "move permission to user settings", "set DEBUG=true", "when claude stops show X". For simple settings like theme/model, suggest the /config command.

commands.name: verify
commands.description: Verify that a code change actually does what it's supposed to by exercising it end-to-end and observing behavior — drive the affected flow, not just tests or typecheck. Run before committing nontrivial changes; bootstraps this repo's project verify skill if none exists yet. Don't invoke it on a diff that only touches tests, docs, or other code with no runtime surface to drive (a change to product source always has one) — there's nothing to observe.

commands.name: debug
commands.description: Enable debug logging for this session and help diagnose issues

commands.name: code-review
commands.description: Review the current diff, or a PR number/branch/path target, for correctness bugs (plus reuse/simplification/efficiency cleanups where the model's review recipe covers them) at the given effort level (low|medium|high|xhigh|max: from few high-confidence findings up to many, some of them uncertain; ultra: deep multi-agent review in the cloud); with no level given, it reuses the level you typed last. Pass --comment to post findings as inline PR comments, or --fix to apply the findings to the working tree after the review. Pass --max-findings <n> to report up to n findings, or --max-findings all for every finding. The choice stays until you pass --max-findings default. For ultra on a GitHub.com PR target, --post asks to post the finished review’s findings to the PR as a single comment from the user’s GitHub account (not a review; the launch dialog still confirms in interactive sessions, while non-interactive mode posts on the flag alone) and --no-post hides that option.

commands.name: simplify
commands.description: Review the changed code for reuse, simplification, efficiency, and altitude cleanups, then apply the fixes. Quality only — it does not hunt for bugs; use /code-review for that.

commands.name: batch
commands.description: Research and plan a large-scale change, then execute it in parallel across 5–30 isolated worktree agents that each open a PR.

commands.name: fewer-permission-prompts
commands.description: Scan your transcripts for common read-only Bash and MCP tool calls, then add a prioritized allowlist to project .claude/settings.json to reduce permission prompts.

commands.name: doctor
commands.description: Health-check the user's Claude Code setup and fix issues: diagnose installation health — what the `claude doctor` terminal diagnostics cover — from local data (duplicate or leftover installs, PATH, unparseable settings files, broken or colliding agent definitions, skills whose frontmatter fails to parse); find unused skills, MCP servers, and plugins versus their context cost and disable dead weight; deduplicate local CLAUDE.md files against checked-in ones; trim checked-in CLAUDE.md files by cutting content a session could derive from the codebase (directory layouts, tech-stack lists, architecture overviews) while keeping gotchas, rationale, and non-standard conventions; migrate always-loaded CLAUDE.md guidance into lazy skills and nested CLAUDE.md files; flag slow hooks and context-heavy extensions; check the installed version is current; make auto mode the default permission mode; and pre-approve frequently denied read-only commands. Use when the user asks for a doctor run, checkup, audit, tune-up, or cleanup of their Claude Code setup or configuration.

commands.name: loop
commands.description: Run a prompt or slash command on a recurring interval (e.g. /loop 5m /foo). Omit the interval to let the model self-pace.

commands.name: schedule
commands.description: Create, update, list, or run scheduled cloud agents (routines) that execute on a cron schedule.

commands.name: claude-api
commands.description:
Reference for the Claude API / Anthropic SDK — model ids, pricing, params, streaming, tool use, MCP, agents, caching, token counting, model migration.
TRIGGER — read BEFORE opening the target file; don't skip because it "looks like a one-liner" — whenever: the prompt names Claude/Anthropic in any form (Claude, Anthropic, Fable, Opus, Sonnet, Haiku, `anthropic`, `@anthropic-ai`, `claude-*`, `us.anthropic.*`, `[1m]`); the user asks about an LLM (pricing/model choice/limits/caching) — never answer from memory; OR the task is LLM-shaped with provider unstated (agent/MCP/tool-definition/multi-agent/RAG/LLM-judge/computer-use; generate/summarize/extract/classify/rewrite/converse over NL; debugging refusals/cutoffs/streaming/tool-calls/tokens).
SKIP only when another provider is being worked on (overrides all triggers): OpenAI/GPT/Gemini/Llama/Mistral/Cohere/Ollama named in the query; OR `grep -rE 'openai|langchain_openai|google.generativeai|genai|mistralai|cohere|ollama'` over the project hits (run this grep FIRST if no provider named — don't Read the file).

commands.name: workflow-authoring
commands.description: Reference for writing a Workflow tool script (script API and gotchas, resume, quality patterns, worked examples). Load before authoring a script for a workflow the user already opted into; it does not itself authorize running one.

commands.name: run
commands.description: Launch and drive this project's app to see a change working. Use when asked to run, start, or screenshot the app, or to confirm a change works in the real app (not just tests). First looks for a project skill that already covers launching the app; otherwise falls back to built-in patterns per project type (CLI, server, TUI, Electron, browser-driven, library).

commands.name: run-skill-generator
commands.description: Author or improve the run-<unit> skill - a per-project skill that tells agents how to build, launch, and drive this project's app. Use when the user asks to set up the project, get it running, write run instructions, or verify build/run steps work from a clean environment.

commands.name: agents
commands.description: (removed) Ask Claude to create/manage subagents, or edit .claude/agents/

input.content: # Spec (verbatim from user) Build a meeting-room booking app: an HTTP server `server.mjs` (an ES module, run as `node server.mjs`) that serves a JSON API and a browser page, and keeps its data in one JSON file. Server - At startup the server checks `PORT`, then reads the data file, then starts listening, in that order. - It listens on 127.0.0.1 at the port in the `PORT` environment variable. An unset or empty `PORT` means 3000. A `PORT` that is not made only of ASCII digits 0-9, or whose value is above 65535, or a port that cannot be bound (for example because it is in use), makes the server write one line of its choice to stderr and exit with code 1. - Once listening, it prints `listening on http://127.0.0.1:` followed by "\n" to stdout, where `` is the port actually bound (with `PORT=0`, the port the OS picked). This line is the only thing the server ever writes to stdout. - Its data lives in the file named by the `DATA_FILE` environment variable, as JSON in a layout of your choice. An unset or empty `DATA_FILE` means `bookings.json`. A relative `DATA_FILE`, the default included, is resolved against the current working directory, not the folder of `server.mjs`. - The server reads the data file once, at startup. If reading it fails with `ENOENT` (the file, or a folder on its path, does not exist), there are no bookings yet. If reading it fails in any other way (for example the path is a directory), or its content is not data in the layout this server writes (for example it is empty or not valid JSON), the server writes `cannot read data file ` followed by "\n" to stderr, where `` is the value of `DATA_FILE` as given (`bookings.json` when it is unset or empty), and exits with code 1 without listening. - After startup the server's memory is the truth: changes made to the file from outside are not noticed. The server writes the data file only when a POST creates a booking or a DELETE removes one, never at startup or for any other request, and it never creates folders. - Every change is saved to the data file before its reply is sent: after a restart with the same `DATA_FILE`, the bookings, and the id the next booking will get, are as before. - If saving a change fails (for example because the data file's folder does not exist), the reply is 500 `internal error` and nothing changes, the next id included. Any other unexpected failure while handling a request also replies 500 `internal error`. In both cases the server keeps running. - Requests that arrive at the same time give the same result as if they had been handled one at a time in some order: of several overlapping bookings sent at once while saving works, exactly one is created and every other one gets 409, and no id is given twice. - Before sending any reply, the server reads the whole request body, if there is one, and discards what it does not use, so the client always receives the reply, the 413 and 415 replies included. API - The rooms are fixed: `Aurora`, `Borealis` and `Cosmos`, in that order. - A booking is a JSON object with exactly the keys `id`, `room`, `title`, `date`, `start` and `end`: `id` is a number, the others are strings. The first booking gets id 1 and each new booking the next integer; an id is never reused, even after deletes and restarts. - Only the parsed JSON of a reply body matters: whitespace and key order in it are free. - A request's path is its request target up to the first `?` (all of it when there is no `?`). Routes compare the path byte for byte, with no percent-decoding and no dot-segment, slash or letter-case normalisation: `/api/%62ookings`, `/api/./rooms`, `/API/rooms` and `/api/bookings/` are none of the paths below. The query, the text after the first `?`, is ignored unless stated, and is decoded as `new URLSearchParams(query)` does. - `GET /api/rooms`: 200 `{"rooms": ["Aurora", "Borealis", "Cosmos"]}`. - `GET /api/bookings`: 200 `{"bookings": [...]}` with every booking, sorted by date, then start, then room in the order above. When the query has a `date` parameter (as `params.has('date')` says; `?date` with no `=` counts, with the empty value), its value is `params.get('date')` (the first one when repeated) and the reply holds only the bookings on that date; a value that is not a valid date by rule 6 below (the empty value included) gets 400 `date must be a valid YYYY-MM-DD date`. Other query parameters are ignored. - `POST /api/bookings` with a JSON body holding `room`, `title`, `date`, `start` and `end`: 201 and the new booking. Other keys in the body are ignored. - `DELETE /api/bookings/`: every path that is `/api/bookings/` followed by a non-empty `` holding no `/` is this route, whatever `` is. The reply is 204 with an empty body, and the booking is gone. When `` is not a positive integer written in ASCII digits 0-9 without a leading zero, or no booking has that id: 404 `booking not found`. - `GET /` and `GET /app.js` serve the page (see Page). - Any other path: 404 `not found`, whatever the method. For example `GET /api/bookings/abc` is 405. A 405 reply may or may not have an `Allow` header; it is not checked. - Every reply with a body other than the page and the script has `Content-Type: application/json; charset=utf-8`. An error reply is `{"error": ""}` with exactly that key, where `` is the text given here. Booking rules (`POST /api/bookings`; the first rule that fails decides the reply) 1. The media type of the `Content-Type` header (the part before the first `;`, with spaces and tabs removed from both ends, letter case ignored) is not `application/json`, or the header is missing: 415 `content type must be application/json`. 2. The body is longer than 10000 bytes, counting the body bytes actually received: 413 `body too large`. 3. The body, decoded as `Buffer.prototype.toString('utf8')` does and then given to `JSON.parse`, is not a JSON object (it is empty, not valid JSON, `null`, an array, a string, a number or a boolean): 400 `body must be a JSON object`. Bytes that are not valid UTF-8 become U+FFFD and are not an error by themselves. A byte order mark at the very start is kept, so such a body is not valid JSON. 4. `room` is not a string equal to one of the room names (letter case matters): 400 `room must be one of Aurora, Borealis, Cosmos`. 5. `title` is not a string, or is shorter than 1 or longer than 80 UTF-16 code units after removing the whitespace at both ends (as `String.prototype.trim` does): 400 `title must be 1 to 80 characters`. The booking keeps the trimmed title. 6. `date` is not a string `YYYY-MM-DD` (4, 2 and 2 ASCII digits 0-9) naming a real day from 2000-01-01 to 2099-12-31, where February has 29 days in years divisible by 4: 400 `date must be a valid YYYY-MM-DD date`. 7. `start` is not a string `HH:MM` (2 and 2 ASCII digits 0-9) from `00:00` to `23:59`: 400 `start must be HH:MM`. 8. `end` is not such a string: 400 `end must be HH:MM`. 9. `end` is not later than `start`: 400 `end must be after start`. 10. The booking overlaps a booking of the same room on the same date, that is each of the two starts before the other ends (a booking may start exactly when another ends): 409 `room is already booked from to `, with the start and end of the overlapping booking that starts earliest. - No field except `title` is trimmed or changed: ` 2026-11-03`, `2026-11-3` and `9:00` are invalid. decisions.md — supervisor — file layout, ownership, data file layout, package.json — 2026-11-02
# Spec (verbatim from user)

Build a meeting-room booking app: an HTTP server `server.mjs` (an ES module, run as `node server.mjs`) that serves a JSON API and a browser page, and keeps its data in one JSON file.

Server
- At startup the server checks `PORT`, then reads the data file, then starts listening, in that order.
- It listens on 127.0.0.1 at the port in the `PORT` environment variable. An unset or empty `PORT` means 3000. A `PORT` that is not made only of ASCII digits 0-9, or whose value is above 65535, or a port that cannot be bound (for example because it is in use), makes the server write one line of its choice to stderr and exit with code 1.
- Once listening, it prints `listening on http://127.0.0.1:<port>` followed by "\n" to stdout, where `<port>` is the port actually bound (with `PORT=0`, the port the OS picked). This line is the only thing the server ever writes to stdout.
- Its data lives in the file named by the `DATA_FILE` environment variable, as JSON in a layout of your choice. An unset or empty `DATA_FILE` means `bookings.json`. A relative `DATA_FILE`, the default included, is resolved against the current working directory, not the folder of `server.mjs`.
- The server reads the data file once, at startup. If reading it fails with `ENOENT` (the file, or a folder on its path, does not exist), there are no bookings yet. If reading it fails in any other way (for example the path is a directory), or its content is not data in the layout this server writes (for example it is empty or not valid JSON), the server writes `cannot read data file <name>` followed by "\n" to stderr, where `<name>` is the value of `DATA_FILE` as given (`bookings.json` when it is unset or empty), and exits with code 1 without listening.
- After startup the server's memory is the truth: changes made to the file from outside are not noticed. The server writes the data file only when a POST creates a booking or a DELETE removes one, never at startup or for any other request, and it never creates folders.
- Every change is saved to the data file before its reply is sent: after a restart with the same `DATA_FILE`, the bookings, and the id the next booking will get, are as before.
- If saving a change fails (for example because the data file's folder does not exist), the reply is 500 `internal error` and nothing changes, the next id included. Any other unexpected failure while handling a request also replies 500 `internal error`. In both cases the server keeps running.
- Requests that arrive at the same time give the same result as if they had been handled one at a time in some order: of several overlapping bookings sent at once while saving works, exactly one is created and every other one gets 409, and no id is given twice.
- Before sending any reply, the server reads the whole request body, if there is one, and discards what it does not use, so the client always receives the reply, the 413 and 415 replies included.

API
- The rooms are fixed: `Aurora`, `Borealis` and `Cosmos`, in that order.
- A booking is a JSON object with exactly the keys `id`, `room`, `title`, `date`, `start` and `end`: `id` is a number, the others are strings. The first booking gets id 1 and each new booking the next integer; an id is never reused, even after deletes and restarts.
- Only the parsed JSON of a reply body matters: whitespace and key order in it are free.
- A request's path is its request target up to the first `?` (all of it when there is no `?`). Routes compare the path byte for byte, with no percent-decoding and no dot-segment, slash or letter-case normalisation: `/api/%62ookings`, `/api/./rooms`, `/API/rooms` and `/api/bookings/` are none of the paths below. The query, the text after the first `?`, is ignored unless stated, and is decoded as `new URLSearchParams(query)` does.
- `GET /api/rooms`: 200 `{"rooms": ["Aurora", "Borealis", "Cosmos"]}`.
- `GET /api/bookings`: 200 `{"bookings": [...]}` with every booking, sorted by date, then start, then room in the order above. When the query has a `date` parameter (as `params.has('date')` says; `?date` with no `=` counts, with the empty value), its value is `params.get('date')` (the first one when repeated) and the reply holds only the bookings on that date; a value that is not a valid date by rule 6 below (the empty value included) gets 400 `date must be a valid YYYY-MM-DD date`. Other query parameters are ignored.
- `POST /api/bookings` with a JSON body holding `room`, `title`, `date`, `start` and `end`: 201 and the new booking. Other keys in the body are ignored.
- `DELETE /api/bookings/<id>`: every path that is `/api/bookings/` followed by a non-empty `<id>` holding no `/` is this route, whatever `<id>` is. The reply

... [5684 characters truncated] ...

s no reply. A request that gets no reply at all (for example because the server is down) shows `Could not reach the server.` in `#error`, except for an earlier list fetch, as said below.
- Rooms: the HTML holds no `<option>` element and none of the room names. When the page loads, the script requests `GET /api/rooms` and fills `#room` with one `<option>` per room, in that order, whose value and text are the room name. If that request gets an error status, `#error` shows the reply's error message and `#room` stays empty; with no reply, `#error` shows `Could not reach the server.` and `#room` stays empty. The first list fetch starts at page load too, without waiting for the rooms reply.
- The list: when the page loads, and each time the Page rules say the list is fetched again, the script requests `GET /api/bookings`, adding `?date=<value>` (the value unchanged) while the value of `#filter-date` is not empty, and replaces the content of `#booking-list` with one `<li>` per booking in the reply's order. Each `<li>` has exactly two child nodes: a text node with exactly the text `<date> <start>-<end> <room>: <title>` and no trailing space (for example `2026-11-03 09:00-10:00 Aurora: Standup`), then a `<button type="button">` with the text `Cancel`. With no bookings, the list holds a single `<li>` whose only child is a text node `No bookings.`.
- A list fetch that gets an error status shows the reply's error message in `#error` and leaves the list as it was; one that gets no reply shows `Could not reach the server.` and leaves the list as it was; one that succeeds leaves `#error` alone. When list fetches overlap, only the outcome of the last one started is used: the outcome of every earlier one, an error status or no reply included, changes neither the list nor `#error`.
- Booking: a submit event on the form never reloads the page (the script calls `preventDefault`). A submit while `Book` is disabled sends nothing. Otherwise the script disables `Book`, then sends `POST /api/bookings` with exactly the header `Content-Type: application/json` and a JSON body whose keys `room`, `title`, `date`, `start` and `end` hold the five controls' current values unchanged (the title is not trimmed). The script never checks the fields itself. `Book` is enabled again as soon as the request settles (the reply and its body have arrived, or the request failed), before anything else happens. On 201 the `title` control is emptied (the others keep their values), `#error` is emptied and the list is fetched again. On any other status `#error` shows the reply's error message exactly (for example `room is already booked from 09:00 to 10:00`). With no reply `#error` shows `Could not reach the server.`. In both of these cases the form and the list stay as they were.
- Cancel: clicking a `Cancel` button disables it and sends `DELETE /api/bookings/<id>` for its booking; the button is enabled again when the request settles. On 204 `#error` is emptied; on any other status `#error` shows the reply's error message (for example `booking not found` when the booking was already gone). After either of these, the list is fetched again. With no reply, `#error` shows `Could not reach the server.` and the list is not fetched again.
- Filter: a `change` event on `#filter-date` fetches the list again at once; the `input` event does nothing. `Show all` sets the value of `#filter-date` to the empty string and fetches the list again once, without dispatching any event.

Also add tests with node:test, a `package.json` ("type": "module", a "start" script that runs `node server.mjs`, and a "test" script), and a README with usage.
# Decisions (supervisor)

- Full user spec: see `.team/notes/spec.md` (exact, final; every value in it is exact).
- Only Node.js built-ins, no npm install. Node 22. Tests use `node:test`.
- File layout:
  - `server.mjs` — backend (HTTP server, JSON API, data file). Owner: backend.
  - `public/index.html` and `public/app.js` — the page and its classic script. Owner: frontend.
    `server.mjs` reads both from `new URL('./public/…', import.meta.url)` (relative to server.mjs, NOT cwd)
    per request or at startup (backend's choice) and serves them on `GET /` and `GET /app.js`.
  - `test/server.test.mjs` — backend tests (owner backend). `test/app.test.mjs` — frontend tests
    (owner frontend; run app.js in `node:vm` with a fake DOM + fake fetch, and check index.html markup).
  - `package.json`: `{"type":"module","scripts":{"start":"node server.mjs","test":"node --test test/"}}`. Owner: backend.
  - `README.md` — owner docs.
- Data file layout: `{"nextId": <int>, "bookings": [ ...booking objects ]}` (backend owns; validate on load strictly).

Build a meeting-room booking app: an HTTP server `server.mjs` (an ES module, run as `node server.mjs`) that serves a JSON API and a browser page, and keeps its data in one JSON file.

Server
- At startup the server checks `PORT`, then reads the data file, then starts listening, in that order.
- It listens on 127.0.0.1 at the port in the `PORT` environment variable. An unset or empty `PORT` means 3000. A `PORT` that is not made only of ASCII digits 0-9, or whose value is above 65535, or a port that cannot be bound (for example because it is in use), makes the server write one line of its choice to stderr and exit with code 1.
- Once listening, it prints `listening on http://127.0.0.1:<port>` followed by "\n" to stdout, where `<port>` is the port actually bound (with `PORT=0`, the port the OS picked). This line is the only thing the server ever writes to stdout.
- Its data lives in the file named by the `DATA_FILE` environment variable, as JSON in a layout of your choice. An unset or empty `DATA_FILE` means `bookings.json`. A relative `DATA_FILE`, the default included, is resolved against the current working directory, not the folder of `server.mjs`.
- The server reads the data file once, at startup. If reading it fails with `ENOENT` (the file, or a folder on its path, does not exist), there are no bookings yet. If reading it fails in any other way (for example the path is a directory), or its content is not data in the layout this server writes (for example it is empty or not valid JSON), the server writes `cannot read data file <name>` followed by "\n" to stderr, where `<name>` is the value of `DATA_FILE` as given (`bookings.json` when it is unset or empty), and exits with code 1 without listening.
- After startup the server's memory is the truth: changes made to the file from outside are not noticed. The server writes the data file only when a POST creates a booking or a DELETE removes one, never at startup or for any other request, and it never creates folders.
- Every change is saved to the data file before its reply is sent: after a restart with the same `DATA_FILE`, the bookings, and the id the next booking will get, are as before.
- If saving a change fails (for example because the data file's folder does not exist), the reply is 500 `internal error` and nothing changes, the next id included. Any other unexpected failure while handling a request also replies 500 `internal error`. In both cases the server keeps running.
- Requests that arrive at the same time give the same result as if they had been handled one at a time in some order: of several overlapping bookings sent at once while saving works, exactly one is created and every other one gets 409, and no id is given twice.
- Before sending any reply, the server reads the whole request body, if there is one, and discards what it does not use, so the client always receives the reply, the 413 and 415 replies included.

API
- The rooms are fixed: `Aurora`, `Borealis` and `Cosmos`, in that order.
- A booking is a JSON object with exactly the keys `id`, `room`, `title`, `date`, `start` and `end`: `id` is a number, the others are strings. The first booking gets id 1 and each new booking the next integer; an id is never reused, even after deletes and restarts.

Other query parameters are ignored.

- `DELETE /api/bookings/<id>`: every path that is `/api/bookings/` followed by a non-empty `<id>` holding no `/` is this route, whatever `<id>` is. The reply

In both of these cases the form and the list stay as they were.
- Cancel: clicking a `Cancel` button disables it and sends `DELETE /api/bookings/<id>` for its booking; the button is enabled again when the request settles. On 204 `#error` is emptied; on any other status `#error` shows the reply's error message (for example `booking not found` when the booking was already gone). After either of these, the list is fetched again. With no reply, `#error` shows `Could not reach the server.` and the list is not fetched again.
- Filter: a `change` event on `#filter-date` fetches the list again at once; the `input` event does nothing. `Show all` sets the value of `#filter-date` to the empty string and fetches the list again once, without dispatching any event.

  - `README.md` — owner docs.

# Spec (verbatim from user)

Build a meeting-room booking app: an HTTP server `server.mjs` (an ES module, run as `node server.mjs`) that serves a JSON API and a browser page, and keeps its data in one JSON file.

Server
- At startup the server checks `PORT`, then reads the data file, then starts listening, in that order.
- It listens on 127.0.0.1 at the port in the `PORT` environment variable. An unset or empty `PORT` means 3000. A `PORT` that is not made only of ASCII digits 0-9, or whose value is above 65535, or a port that cannot be bound (for example because it is in use), makes the server write one line of its choice to stderr and exit with code 1.
- Once listening, it prints `listening on http://127.0.0.1:<port>` followed by "\n" to stdout, where `<port>` is the port actually bound (with `PORT=0`, the port the OS picked). This line is the only thing the server ever writes to stdout.
- Its data lives in the file named by the `DATA_FILE` environment variable, as JSON in a layout of your choice. An unset or empty `DATA_FILE` means `bookings.json`. A relative `DATA_FILE`, the default included, is resolved against the current working directory, not the folder of `server.mjs`.
- The server reads the data file once, at startup. If reading it fails with `ENOENT` (the file, or a folder on its path, does not exist), there are no bookings yet. If reading it fails in any other way (for example the path is a directory), or its content is not data in the layout this server writes (for example it is empty or not valid JSON), the server writes `cannot read data file <name>` followed by "\n" to stderr, where `<name>` is the value of `DATA_FILE` as given (`bookings.json` when it is unset or empty), and exits with code 1 without listening.
- After startup the server's memory is the truth: changes made to the file from outside are not noticed. The server writes the data file only when a POST creates a booking or a DELETE removes one, never at startup or for any other request, and it never creates folders.
- Every change is saved to the data file before its reply is sent: after a restart with the same `DATA_FILE`, the bookings, and the id the next booking will get, are as before.
- If saving a change fails (for example because the data file's folder does not exist), the reply is 500 `internal error` and nothing changes, the next id included. Any other unexpected failure while handling a request also replies 500 `internal error`. In both cases the server keeps running.
- Requests that arrive at the same time give the same result as if they had been handled one at a time in some order: of several overlapping bookings sent at once while saving works, exactly one is created and every other one gets 409, and no id is given twice.
- Before sending any reply, the server reads the whole request body, if there is one, and discards what it does not use, so the client always receives the reply, the 413 and 415 replies included.

API
- The rooms are fixed: `Aurora`, `Borealis` and `Cosmos`, in that order.
- A booking is a JSON object with exactly the keys `id`, `room`, `title`, `date`, `start` and `end`: `id` is a number, the others are strings. The first booking gets id 1 and each new booking the next integer; an id is never reused, even after deletes and restarts.
- Only the parsed JSON of a reply body matters: whitespace and key order in it are free.
- A request's path is its request target up to the first `?` (all of it when there is no `?`). Routes compare the path byte for byte, with no percent-decoding and no dot-segment, slash or letter-case normalisation: `/api/%62ookings`, `/api/./rooms`, `/API/rooms` and `/api/bookings/` are none of the paths below. The query, the text after the first `?`, is ignored unless stated, and is decoded as `new URLSearchParams(query)` does.
- `GET /api/rooms`: 200 `{"rooms": ["Aurora", "Borealis", "Cosmos"]}`.
- `GET /api/bookings`: 200 `{"bookings": [...]}` with every booking, sorted by date, then start, then room in the order above. When the query has a `date` parameter (as `params.has('date')` says; `?date` with no `=` counts, with the empty value), its value is `params.get('date')` (the first one when repeated) and the reply holds only the bookings on that date; a value that is not a valid date by rule 6 below (the empty value included) gets 400 `date must be a valid YYYY-MM-DD date`. Other query parameters are ignored.
- `POST /api/bookings` with a JSON body holding `room`, `title`, `date`, `start` and `end`: 201 and the new booking. Other keys in the body are ignored.
- `DELETE /api/bookings/<id>`: every path that is `/api/bookings/` followed by a non-empty `<id>` holding no `/` is this route, whatever `<id>` is. The reply

... [5709 characters truncated] ...

t gets no reply at all (for example because the server is down) shows `Could not reach the server.` in `#error`, except for an earlier list fetch, as said below.
- Rooms: the HTML holds no `<option>` element and none of the room names. When the page loads, the script requests `GET /api/rooms` and fills `#room` with one `<option>` per room, in that order, whose value and text are the room name. If that request gets an error status, `#error` shows the reply's error message and `#room` stays empty; with no reply, `#error` shows `Could not reach the server.` and `#room` stays empty. The first list fetch starts at page load too, without waiting for the rooms reply.
- The list: when the page loads, and each time the Page rules say the list is fetched again, the script requests `GET /api/bookings`, adding `?date=<value>` (the value unchanged) while the value of `#filter-date` is not empty, and replaces the content of `#booking-list` with one `<li>` per booking in the reply's order. Each `<li>` has exactly two child nodes: a text node with exactly the text `<date> <start>-<end> <room>: <title>` and no trailing space (for example `2026-11-03 09:00-10:00 Aurora: Standup`), then a `<button type="button">` with the text `Cancel`. With no bookings, the list holds a single `<li>` whose only child is a text node `No bookings.`.
- A list fetch that gets an error status shows the reply's error message in `#error` and leaves the list as it was; one that gets no reply shows `Could not reach the server.` and leaves the list as it was; one that succeeds leaves `#error` alone. When list fetches overlap, only the outcome of the last one started is used: the outcome of every earlier one, an error status or no reply included, changes neither the list nor `#error`.
- Booking: a submit event on the form never reloads the page (the script calls `preventDefault`). A submit while `Book` is disabled sends nothing. Otherwise the script disables `Book`, then sends `POST /api/bookings` with exactly the header `Content-Type: application/json` and a JSON body whose keys `room`, `title`, `date`, `start` and `end` hold the five controls' current values unchanged (the title is not trimmed). The script never checks the fields itself. `Book` is enabled again as soon as the request settles (the reply and its body have arrived, or the request failed), before anything else happens. On 201 the `title` control is emptied (the others keep their values), `#error` is emptied and the list is fetched again. On any other status `#error` shows the reply's error message exactly (for example `room is already booked from 09:00 to 10:00`). With no reply `#error` shows `Could not reach the server.`. In both of these cases the form and the list stay as they were.
- Cancel: clicking a `Cancel` button disables it and sends `DELETE /api/bookings/<id>` for its booking; the button is enabled again when the request settles. On 204 `#error` is emptied; on any other status `#error` shows the reply's error message (for example `booking not found` when the booking was already gone). After either of these, the list is fetched again. With no reply, `#error` shows `Could not reach the server.` and the list is not fetched again.
- Filter: a `change` event on `#filter-date` fetches the list again at once; the `input` event does nothing. `Show all` sets the value of `#filter-date` to the empty string and fetches the list again once, without dispatching any event.

- Full user spec: see `.team/notes/spec.md` (exact, final; every value in it is exact).
- Only Node.js built-ins, no npm install. Node 22. Tests use `node:test`.
- File layout:

  - `public/index.html` and `public/app.js` — the page and its classic script. Owner: frontend.
    `server.mjs` reads both from `new URL('./public/…', import.meta.url)` (relative to server.mjs, NOT cwd)
    per request or at startup (backend's choice) and serves them on `GET /` and `GET /app.js`.
  - `test/server.test.mjs` — backend tests (owner backend). `test/app.test.mjs` — frontend tests
    (owner frontend; run app.js in `node:vm` with a fake DOM + fake fetch, and check index.html markup).
  - `package.json`: `{"type":"module","scripts":{"start":"node server.mjs","test":"node --test test/"}}`. Owner: backend.
  - `README.md` — owner docs.
- Data file layout: `{"nextId": <int>, "bookings": [ ...booking objects ]}` (backend owns; validate on load strictly).

# Room bookings

A small meeting-room booking app. `server.mjs` is a Node.js HTTP server. It serves a JSON API and a browser page, and it keeps its bookings in a single JSON file.

There are three fixed rooms: `Aurora`, `Borealis` and `Cosmos`. Bookings are made per room, per date, with a start and end time, and two bookings of the same room may not overlap.

## Requirements

- Node.js 22 or later.
- Nothing else. The app uses only Node.js built-ins, so there is no `npm install` step.

## Usage

```sh
npm start
# or
node server.mjs
```

Then open http://127.0.0.1:3000 in a browser.

The server listens on `127.0.0.1` only. Once it is listening it prints exactly one line to stdout:

```
listening on http://127.0.0.1:3000
```

Nothing else is ever written to stdout.

### Environment variables

| Variable    | Default         | Meaning |
|-------------|-----------------|---------|
| `PORT`      | `3000`          | Port to listen on. If it is unset or empty, `3000` is used. `PORT=0` lets the OS pick a free port, and the printed line shows the port that was actually bound. |
| `DATA_FILE` | `bookings.json` | Path of the data file. If it is unset or empty, `bookings.json` is used. A relative path is resolved against the current working directory, not the folder that holds `server.mjs`. |

```sh
PORT=8080 DATA_FILE=/var/lib/rooms/bookings.json node server.mjs
```

### Startup and errors

At startup the server checks `PORT` first, then reads the data file, then starts listening.

- **Bad `PORT`**: if `PORT` contains anything other than the ASCII digits 0-9, is above 65535, or cannot be bound (for example because the port is in use), the server writes one error line to stderr and exits with code 1.
- **Missing data file**: if the file, or a folder on its path, does not exist, the server starts with no bookings. It does not create the file at startup.
- **Unreadable or invalid data file**: if the file cannot be read for any other reason (for example the path is a directory), or its content is not in the layout described under [Data file](#data-file) (for example it is empty or not valid JSON), the server writes the line below to stderr and exits with code 1 without listening. `<name>` is `DATA_FILE` exactly as given, or `bookings.json` when it is unset.

  ```
  cannot read data file <name>
  ```

## API

Every reply body is JSON with `Content-Type: application/json; charset=utf-8`. The only exceptions are the page and its script. Error replies look like `{"error": "<message>"}`.

| Method   | Path                    | Success                         |
|----------|-------------------------|---------------------------------|
| `GET`    | `/api/rooms`            | 200 `{"rooms": ["Aurora", "Borealis", "Cosmos"]}` |
| `GET`    | `/api/bookings`         | 200 `{"bookings": [...]}`       |
| `POST`   | `/api/bookings`         | 201 and the new booking         |
| `DELETE` | `/api/bookings/<id>`    | 204, empty body                 |
| `GET`    | `/`                     | 200, the page (`text/html; charset=utf-8`) |
| `GET`    | `/app.js`               | 200, the page's script (`text/javascript; charset=utf-8`) |

### Routing

- The path is the request target up to the first `?`. It is compared byte for byte, with no percent-decoding and no normalisation of case, slashes or dot-segments. So `/API/rooms`, `/api/./rooms`, `/api/%62ookings` and `/api/bookings/` do not match any route.
- Any other path returns 404 `not found`, whatever the method. This includes `/api/bookings/` and `/api/bookings/1/`.
- A known path with a method it does not support (HEAD and OPTIONS included) returns 405 `method not allowed`. For example, `GET /api/bookings/abc` returns 405.
- The query string is ignored, except for `date` on `GET /api/bookings`.

### Bookings

A booking has exactly these keys:

```json
{ "id": 1, "room": "Aurora", "title": "Standup", "date": "2026-11-03", "start": "09:00", "end": "10:00" }
```

`id` is a number. The first booking gets 1 and each new booking gets the next integer. An id is never reused, even after deletes and restarts.

#### `GET /api/bookings`

Returns every booking, sorted by date, then start, then room (in the order Aurora, Borealis, Cosmos).

`?date=YYYY-MM-DD` returns only the bookings on that date. If `date` is present (even as `?date` with no value) and is not a valid date under the rules below, the reply is 400 `date must be a valid YYYY-MM-DD date`. If `date` is repeated, the first value is used. Other query parameters are ignored.

#### `POST /api/bookings`

The body is a JSON object with `room`, `title`, `date`, `start` and `end`. Other keys are ignored. The checks run in this order, and the first one that fails decides the reply:

| # | Rule | Reply |
|---|------|-------|
| 1 | The `Content-Type` media type must be `application/json` (case-insensitive; parameters such as `; charset=utf-8` are allowed) | 415 `content type must be application/json` |
| 2 | The body must be at most 10000 bytes | 413 `body too large` |
| 3 | The body must parse as a JSON object (not empty, `null`, an array or another non-object value) | 400 `body must be a JSON object` |
| 4 | `room` must be exactly `Aurora`, `Borealis` or `Cosmos` (case-sensitive) | 400 `room must be one of Aurora, Borealis, Cosmos` |
| 5 | `title` must be a string of 1 to 80 characters after trimming whitespace from both ends. The trimmed title is the one stored | 400 `title must be 1 to 80 characters` |
| 6 | `date` must be `YYYY-MM-DD` and a real day from 2000-01-01 to 2099-12-31 | 400 `date must be a valid YYYY-MM-DD date` |
| 7 | `start` must be `HH:MM` from `00:00` to `23:59` | 400 `start must be HH:MM` |
| 8 | `end` must be `HH:MM` from `00:00` to `23:59` | 400 `end must be HH:MM` |
| 9 | `end` must be later than `start` | 400 `end must be after start` |
| 10 | The booking must not overlap another booking of the same room on the same date. Back-to-back bookings are fine | 409 `room is already booked from <start> to <end>` (the earliest-starting overlapping booking) |

Only `title` is trimmed. Other fields must match exactly, so ` 2026-11-03`, `2026-11-3` and `9:00` are rejected.

#### `DELETE /api/bookings/<id>`

Deletes the booking and returns 204 with an empty body. If `<id>` is not a positive integer without a leading zero, or no booking has that id, the reply is 404 `booking not found`.

#### Server errors

If saving the data file fails (for example because its folder does not exist), the reply is 500 `internal error` and nothing changes, including the next id. Any other unexpected failure also returns 500 `internal error`. In both cases the server keeps running.

Requests that arrive at the same time give the same result as if they had been handled one after another. If several overlapping bookings are sent at once, exactly one is created and the others get 409.

### Examples

```sh
curl http://127.0.0.1:3000/api/rooms

curl -X POST http://127.0.0.1:3000/api/bookings \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -d '{"room":"Aurora","title":"Standup","date":"2026-11-03","start":"09:00","end":"10:00"}'
# 201 {"id":1,"room":"Aurora","title":"Standup","date":"2026-11-03","start":"09:00","end":"10:00"}

curl 'http://127.0.0.1:3000/api/bookings?date=2026-11-03'

curl -i -X DELETE http://127.0.0.1:3000/api/bookings/1
# HTTP/1.1 204 No Content
```

## The page

Open `/` in a browser to use the page. From there you can:

- book a room with the form (room, title, date, start, end). Validation is done by the server, and its error messages appear on the page;
- see the list of bookings, filter it by date with **Show date**, and clear the filter with **Show all**;
- cancel a booking with its **Cancel** button.

If the server cannot be reached, the page shows `Could not reach the server.`

## Data file

The server reads the data file once, at startup. After that its in-memory state is what counts, and changes made to the file from outside are not noticed. The file is written only when a booking is created or deleted, and the write finishes before the reply is sent, so a restart with the same `DATA_FILE` keeps the bookings and the next id. The server never creates folders.

Layout:

```json
{
  "nextId": 2,
  "bookings": [
    { "id": 1, "room": "Aurora", "title": "Standup", "date": "2026-11-03", "start": "09:00", "end": "10:00" }
  ]
}
```

`nextId` is the id the next booking will get. If the file is not in this layout, the server refuses to start (see [Startup and errors](#startup-and-errors)).

## Running tests

```sh
npm test
```

This runs `node --test test/`, which uses the built-in `node:test` runner.

## Project layout

```
server.mjs              HTTP server, JSON API and data file handling
public/index.html       the page
public/app.js           the page's script (served as /app.js)
test/server.test.mjs    API and server tests
test/app.test.mjs       page and script tests
package.json            "type": "module"; start and test scripts
bookings.json           default data file (created on the first booking)
```

summary:
The code passes. I read all four files against the spec and did not run `npm test`. The one problem I found is minor.

**What I checked against the spec**
- **Startup order and exit codes:** `main()` checks `PORT` first, then reads the data file, then listens. Each failure writes one line to stderr and sets exit code 1.
- **Stdout:** the listening line is the only thing written to stdout, and it uses the port actually bound.
- **Data file:** `ENOENT` means no bookings yet, and any other read or parse failure gives `cannot read data file <name>` with the name as given. Relative paths resolve against the current working directory.
- **Routing:**
  - Paths are matched byte for byte after splitting at the first `?`.
  - Fixed routes are checked before the `/api/bookings/<id>` rule, so 405 and 404 come out as specified.
  - Ids that are not canonical positive integers return 404 `booking not found`.
- **Body draining:** `readBody` always consumes the whole body and counts every byte received. The 413 and 415 replies therefore reach the client.
- **Booking rule order:** rules 1 to 10 run in the specified order, and the 409 message reports the earliest-starting overlapping booking.
- **Save and concurrency:**
  - `commit` saves first and swaps in-memory state only if the save succeeds, so a failed save leaves the next id unchanged.
  - Everything after the body is read, the save included, runs synchronously, so requests are serialized.
- **Tests:**
  - They cover PORT edge cases, bad data files, persistence and restart, rollback after a save failure, 10 overlapping POSTs, routing and 405 cases, the 10000/10001 byte boundary, chunked bodies, and rule order.
  - They also cover invalid UTF-8 and a BOM, trimming and UTF-16 title length, leap-year dates, and overlap boundaries.
  - A plausible wrong implementation would fail on these.

**Minor points**
- `server.mjs:130-133`: `sortBookings` uses a nested ternary comparator that is hard to read.
- `server.mjs:41`: `isValidTitle` calls `trim()` twice, and `parseBookingInput` at line 163 trims a third time.
- `server.mjs:226-234` and `server.mjs:237`: handlers are looked up by string name in a `switch`, and `send` is defined after `dispatch` uses it. The indirection adds little.
- `server.mjs:290-293`: the server's `error` handler calls `process.exit(1)` for any server error, which is only correct for listen failures.
- `test/server.test.mjs:529`: `_omit` is an unused variable.
- `test/server.test.mjs`: nothing tests the default `PORT` of 3000, and the page tests skip when `public/` is missing.

## GRADE
Overall: 8.5/10
Verdict: pass

naming: 8 — clear, consistent names (`commit`, `loadState`, `checkContentType`)

size: 9 — server 300 lines, tests 600, every function under 50 lines
errors: 9 — ENOENT told apart from other failures, exact messages and exit codes, save rollback, 500 handling, body always drained
tests: 9 — spec boundaries and wrong-implementation traps covered, including concurrency, rollback and persistence; default port 3000 untested
security: 9 — no injection surface, paths not decoded, own-property reads for body keys, body capped
leftovers: 10 — no console.log, debug code or TODOs

- 2026-11-02 · backend · Concurrency: after the body is fully read, routing, validation, save (`fs.writeFileSync`, no temp file, no mkdir) and state swap run synchronously, so requests are serialized without a lock; state is swapped only after a successful save (rollback incl. nextId) · simplest correct serialization.
- 2026-11-02 · backend · Test helpers live in `test/helpers.mjs` (backend-owned) · keeps test/server.test.mjs under 800 lines.

- Static: `GET /` → public/index.html (`text/html; charset=utf-8`), `GET /app.js` → public/app.js (`text/javascript; charset=utf-8`), read per request relative to server.mjs.
- Endpoints: `GET /api/rooms`, `GET /api/bookings[?date=YYYY-MM-DD]`, `POST /api/bookings`, `DELETE /api/bookings/<id>`.

An unset or empty `PORT` means 3000. A `PORT` that is not made only of ASCII digits 0-9, or whose value is above 65535, or a port that cannot be bound (for example because it is in use), makes the server write one line of its choice to stderr and exit with code 1. 8 - Once listening, it prints `listening on http://127.0.0.1:` followed by "\n" to stdout, where `` is the port actually bound (with `PORT=0`, the port the OS picked). This line is the only thing the server ever writes to stdout. 9 - Its data lives in the file named by the `DATA_FILE` environment variable, as JSON in a layout of your choice. An unset or empty `DATA_FILE` means `bookings.json`. A relative `DATA_FILE`, the default included, is resolved against the current working directory, not the folder of `server.mjs`. 10 - The server reads the data file once, at startup. If reading it fails with `ENOENT` (the file, or a folder on its path, does not exist), there are no bookings yet. If reading it fails in any other way (for example the path is a directory), or its content is not data in the layout this server writes (for example it is empty or not valid JSON), the server writes `cannot read data file ` followed by "\n" to stderr, where `` is the value of `DATA_FILE` as given (`bookings.json` when it is unset or empty), and exits with code 1 without listening. 11 - After startup the server's memory is the truth: changes made to the file from outside are not noticed. The server writes the data file only when a POST creates a booking or a DELETE removes one, never at startup or for any other request, and it never creates folders. 12 - Every change is saved to the data file before its reply is sent: after a restart with the same `DATA_FILE`, the bookings, and the id the next booking will get, are as before. 13 - If saving a change fails (for example because the data file's folder does not exist), the reply is 500 `internal error` and nothing changes, the next id included. Any other unexpected failure while handling a request also replies 500 `internal error`. In both cases the server keeps running. 14 - Requests that arrive at the same time give the same result as if they had been handled one at a time in some order: of several overlapping bookings sent at once while saving works, exactly one is created and every other one gets 409, and no id is given twice. 15 - Before sending any reply, the server reads the whole request body, if there is one, and discards what it does not use, so the client always receives the reply, the 413 and 415 replies included. 16 17 API 18 - The rooms are fixed: `Aurora`, `Borealis` and `Cosmos`, in that order. 19 - A booking is a JSON object with exactly the keys `id`, `room`, `title`, `date`, `start` and `end`: `id` is a number, the others are strings. The first booking gets id 1 and each new booking the next integer; an id is never reused, even after deletes and restarts. 20 - Only the parsed JSON of a reply body matters: whitespace and key order in it are free. 21 - A request's path is its request target up to the first `?` (all of it when there is no `?`). Routes compare the path byte for byte, with no percent-decoding and no dot-segment, slash or letter-case normalisation: `/api/%62ookings`, `/api/./rooms`, `/API/rooms` and `/api/bookings/` are none of the paths below. The query, the text after the first `?`, is ignored unless stated, and is decoded as `new URLSearchParams(query)` does. 22 - `GET /api/rooms`: 200 `{"rooms": ["Aurora", "Borealis", "Cosmos"]}`. 23 - `GET /api/bookings`: 200 `{"bookings": [...]}` with every booking, sorted by date, then start, then room in the order above. When the query has a `date` parameter (as `params.has('date')` says; `?date` with no `=` counts, with the empty value), its value is `params.get('date')` (the first one when repeated) and the reply holds only the bookings on that date; a value that is not a valid date by rule 6 below (the empty value included) gets 400 `date must be a valid YYYY-MM-DD date`. Other query parameters are ignored. 24 - `POST /api/bookings` with a JSON body holding `room`, `title`, `date`, `start` and `end`: 201 and the new booking. Other keys in the body are ignored. 25 - `DELETE /api/bookings/`: every path that is `/api/bookings/` followed by a non-empty `` holding no `/` is this route, whatever `` is. The reply is 204 with an empty body, and the booking is gone. The build fails the spec on one item: a bad `PORT` that contains a line break breaks the one-line stderr rule. Everything else I probed matches the spec. `npm test` gives 125 passed and 4 failed out of 129. The 4 failures are new tests that expose this bug.

**Failing item (owner: backend, agent a95e03794a88e64d0)**
- `/root/bench-runs/h4-788acd71/server.mjs:281` writes `invalid PORT ${process.env.PORT}` to stderr with the raw value. When `PORT` holds a line feed or carriage return, stderr gets more than one line, but the spec allows exactly one. It fails for `PORT="1\n2"`, `"\n"`, `"80\r"` and `"a\r\nb"`.
- The tests that show it are in `/root/bench-runs/h4-788acd71/test/final.test.mjs` (lines 44–51).
- Fix: write a fixed message without echoing the value, or escape it (for example with `JSON.stringify`).
- I treat a lone carriage return as a line break too. That is the stricter reading, and I logged it in `.team/notes/decisions.md`.

**What passed (from reading the code and from tests against the real server)**
- **Startup:**
  - The startup order (`PORT`, then the data file, then listening), the exit codes and stdout holding only the listening line.
  - `PORT=abc`, `65536`, `" 80"`, `+80`, a port already in use and `PORT=0` all behave as specified.
  - The data file being a directory, empty, in an invalid layout, or in a missing folder all behave as specified.
  - A file standing where a folder should be on the path stops startup with `cannot read data file`.
  - An absolute `DATA_FILE` is reported exactly as given.
  - A valid hand-formatted file is not rewritten at startup.
- **Saving and concurrency:**
  - A failed save on POST or DELETE replies 500 `internal error` and leaves the next id unchanged.
  - 30 overlapping bookings sent at once over raw sockets give exactly one 201 and 29 × 409.
- **Large bodies:** 2 MB bodies are read through and the reply still arrives for 200, 404, 405, DELETE 404, 415 and 413.
- **Routing:**
  - HEAD and OPTIONS on every listed path give 405. `OPTIONS *`, an absolute-form target and `/api/rooms#x` give 404.
  - `/api/bookings/%2F` gives 404 `booking not found` on DELETE and 405 on GET. `/api/bookings//` gives 404 `not found`.
  - The query is cut off before routing: `DELETE /api/bookings/1?x=/` gives 204.
  - The DELETE id rules hold for `01`, `0`, `+1` and `1e0`.
- **Validation and listing:**
  - The validation order is right. Leap days work in 2000, 2004 and 2096 and are rejected in 2001 and 2099; 2100 is out of range.
  - The sort order and the `?date` filter are right, including a repeated `date`, `?date` with no value, and `+` decoding to a space.
  - A body that only sets fields through `__proto__` is rejected as missing them.
  - Unicode whitespace is trimmed from titles, and full-width digits in times are rejected.
  - The 409 message names the overlapping booking that starts earliest.
- **Frontend (from reading the code):**
  - It uses only the allowed APIs and contains no `http://` or `https://` strings.
  - The markup matches the spec.
  - When list fetches overlap, only the last one started counts.
  - Book and Cancel are re-enabled once the reply body has arrived, before anything else happens.
  - The error messages, the 204 handling without reading a body, and Show all and the date filter all behave as specified.
  - The existing `test/app.test.mjs` covers all of these.

**Optional (not failures):**
- `/root/bench-runs/h4-788acd71/test/final.test.mjs` bundles several cases per test, so the first failure hides the rest.
- Node's own HTTP parser rejects raw non-ASCII bytes in a request path with 400 before the server sees them. That is outside the app's control.

The meeting-room booking app is built, and `npm test` passes all 132 tests. The page has not been tried in a real browser; its script was tested against a fake page.

- **Server:** `server.mjs` serves the JSON API and the page, and keeps bookings in the data file. Tests start the real server and cover startup errors, the data file surviving a restart, failed saves, simultaneous bookings, routing and every booking rule.
- **Page:** `public/index.html` and `public/app.js`, which `server.mjs` serves at `/` and `/app.js`. Their tests run the script against a fake page.
- **README:** covers running the server, `PORT` and `DATA_FILE`, the API, the data file format and the tests.
- **Final check:** a separate review compared everything with your spec, both by reading the code and by sending real requests to the server. It found one bug: a bad `PORT` containing a line break printed more than one line to stderr. That message is now fixed text that doesn't repeat the value.

Decisions and differences from your spec:
- **Test script:** `package.json` runs `node --test "test/*.test.mjs"`, because `node --test test/` fails on this Node version (22.23). `npm test` is the command to use.
- **Data file:** it holds the next id and the list of bookings. At startup the server rejects any file that isn't exactly in that layout.
- **Page:** if the server answers 200 with a body that isn't the expected list of rooms or bookings, the page shows `Request failed.` and changes nothing. Your spec doesn't cover that case.

One small test-quality issue is left: `test/final.test.mjs` puts several cases in each test, so one failure hides the cases after it.
